steps.summary: Nothing auto-delivered · 2 waiting for a reviewer

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Hey [PERSON_1], [PERSON_2]. Thanks for jumping on. I know we had this on the calendar but appreciate you making time on a Friday.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: So, How's Denver? Getting cold yet?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: It snowed Tuesday. Not a lot, but enough that everyone forgot how to drive. How are you?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: Good, good. Busy week. Before we get into it, I've got [PERSON_4] on from the PreSense product team and [PERSON_5] from support escalations.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: [PERSON_4], [PERSON_5], this is uh, [PERSON_1] and [PERSON_2] from Northwind.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Hi both. Thanks for the time.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_5]
turns.text: Hey. I've been reading through the tickets from the last couple weeks, so I'm roughly up to speed.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Appreciate you both being here. Let's get into it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: [PERSON_1], you want to kick us off?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yeah. So, short version. Since the Genesys update on the third, we're losing PreSense on basically every warm transfer. Not some. Every one.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Okay. When you say losing PreSense, what does the agent actually see? Blank screen pop, wrong data, nothing at all?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Nothing. The screen pop just doesn't fire. Caller gets to the second agent, the Genesys window comes up, and there's no PreSense panel.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: No journey, no ad source, nothing.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: And on a cold transfer, so a straight transfer with no consult, does it fire?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Cold transfers are fine. That's the weird part. It's um, warm transfers specifically. Agent hits consult, talks to the second agent, then completes the transfer, and the pop is gone.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Okay, that's helpful. Uh, Which Genesys version are you on now?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Whatever they pushed on the third. I'd have to pull the exact build. Our platform team manages that. I think it's a 2026 release, but I don't have the number in front of me.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_5]
turns.text: I can grab that from the ticket. I think your platform contact listed it. Was it the cloud release or on-prem?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Cloud. We moved off on-prem two years ago.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_5]
turns.text: Got it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: And is this every queue, or specific ones? Sales queues, service queues, both?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Sales, mostly. Our inbound sales queue. That's where we use PreSense the most. Service uses it less, so honestly I haven't tested service much.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Sales is the one that matters. That's the whole reason we bought it. If a caller clicks an ad, fills out a form, we want the agent to see that before they say hello.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Right. So on the warm transfer, the second agent is in the same queue or a different one?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Different. First agent is a general sales rep, then they consult with a specialist. Fiber specialist, wireless specialist, that kind of thing.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: And the specialist is the one who should get the pop?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yes. The specialist. The first agent already has the context, they're the one who um, took the call. The specialist is cold, they need the journey.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Okay. And when you say the pop doesn't fire, is it that the panel loads empty, or the panel doesn't load at all?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Doesn't load at all. The Genesys screen comes up with the normal stuff, contact record, notes, but the PreSense panel isn't there.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: It's like it never got the data.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_5]
turns.text: Do you have a recent call ID we can look at? Even one from this week?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yeah, I sent a few in the ticket. Um, Tuesday morning, I think three of them. I can send more if that helps.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_5]
turns.text: The three you sent are enough to start. I'll pull the signal logs on those.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: How long does that take? Because we're three uh, weeks in and my team is manually pulling up the customer record before they pick up.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: That's thirty, forty seconds per call. On a thousand calls a day, um, that's real money.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: I get it. That's a real cost. Let me ask one more thing. When the first agent consults, do they use the Genesys consult button, or do they do I mean, something else, like a conference?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Consult button. Standard. That's how we've always done it.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: And it worked before the third? Same flow, same button?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Yes. Nothing changed on our side. That's what's so frustrating. We didn't touch anything, they pushed an update, and now it's broken.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Okay. So the most likely thing is something in how the transfer event gets surfaced to us changed. I don't want to guess at a root cause yet, but the pattern, warm transfer only, different queue, cloud version, points at the transfer signaling.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_5]
turns.text: That matches what I'm seeing in the logs. The PreSense payload is being built, I can see it on the first leg.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_5]
turns.text: It's the handoff to the second leg where it drops.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: So it's on your side?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_5]
turns.text: Not saying that. I'm saying the handoff is where the like, data stops. Whether that's us, Genesys, or the way the two are talking, I need to dig in.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_5]
turns.text: I don't want to point fingers before I know.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Fine. But we need this fixed. My agents are complaining every day.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: And it's not just the agents. I've got my VP asking whether we should even keep PreSense next year if it doesn't survive a transfer.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: [PERSON_2], I hear that. Let's get to a test plan today so we're not sitting on this over the weekend.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Yeah. Here's what I'd like to do. [PERSON_1], can you get me the exact Genesys build number, and a screenshot of the specialist's screen on a warm transfer?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Even a photo of the monitor is fine.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: I can get you the build number. The screenshot is trickier, we have a no-phone-on-the-floor policy, but I can grab a screen capture from the desktop.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: That works. And can you run a a controlled test? One call, warm transfer, same queue, then one warm transfer across queues.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Note the time and the call IDs. That'll tell us if it's queue-specific.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Okay. I can do that Monday morning when the floor's quieter.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_5]
turns.text: Send me uh, the call IDs as soon as you have them and I'll pull the logs in parallel. I'll also open a case with our platform team so it's tracked formally.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Good. Because the ticket I opened has been sitting for a week.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_5]
turns.text: That's on us. I'll own it from here. You'll have my direct line.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: What's the timeline? Realistically.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Uh, if the test confirms what I think, we'll know by Wednesday. Fix depends on what we find. I'm not going to promise a date today.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: I'd rather have a real answer than a fast one. Just keep us in the loop.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: I'll set up a check-in for Wednesday, same time. [PERSON_1], [PERSON_2], anything else before we wrap?

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: No, that's it. Just, please, get this fixed.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_3]
turns.text: We're on it. And hey, good luck with the snow.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_1]
turns.text: Thanks. Talk Wednesday.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_2]
turns.text: Thanks everyone.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_4]
turns.text: Thanks. Bye.

turns.speaker: [PERSON_5]
turns.text: Bye.
